skill_title: Apply Faraday's Law of electromagnetic induction (qualitative)

items.question: What does Faraday's Law of electromagnetic induction state (in words)?
items.expectedAnswer: A changing magnetic flux through a coil induces an EMF.
items.explanation: Faraday: a CHANGE in magnetic flux through a coil induces an EMF.
options: A changing magnetic flux through a coil induces an EMF.
A steady magnetic field induces an EMF.
An electric current always makes a magnet.

items.question: What is needed to induce an EMF in a coil?
items.expectedAnswer: A change in the magnetic flux through the coil.
items.explanation: Induction requires the flux to change; a steady, unchanging flux induces nothing.
options: A change in the magnetic flux through the coil.

items.question: Moving a magnet into a coil induces a current. What happens if the magnet is held still inside the coil?
items.expectedAnswer: No current is induced (no flux change).
items.explanation: A stationary magnet means no change in flux, so no EMF or current is induced.
options: No current is induced (no flux change).

items.question: Moving the magnet faster into the coil produces an induced EMF that is...
items.expectedAnswer: larger.
items.explanation: A faster change of flux gives a larger induced EMF.

items.question: A coil with more turns will have an induced EMF that is...
items.expectedAnswer: larger (for the same flux change).
items.explanation: More turns gives a larger induced EMF for the same rate of flux change.

items.question: Which of these would induce a current in a coil?
items.expectedAnswer: Moving a magnet towards or away from the coil.
items.explanation: Relative motion between the magnet and coil changes the flux and induces a current.
options: Holding a magnet still next to it.
Moving a magnet towards or away from the coil.

items.question: A generator works by...
items.expectedAnswer: rotating a coil in a magnetic field to induce an EMF.
items.explanation: A generator induces an EMF by changing the flux through a rotating coil (electromagnetic induction).
options: rotating a coil in a magnetic field to induce an EMF.
using a battery to make a magnet.

items.question: Electromagnetic induction converts...
items.expectedAnswer: mechanical energy (motion) into electrical energy.
items.explanation: Induction (as in a generator) turns mechanical motion into electrical energy.

items.question: A stronger magnet moved through a coil at the same speed induces an EMF that is...
items.expectedAnswer: larger.
items.explanation: A stronger field means a greater flux change for the same motion, so a larger EMF.

items.question: Induced EMF depends on the RATE of change of flux. This means EMF is larger when the flux changes...
items.expectedAnswer: more quickly.
items.explanation: Faster (quicker) flux change → larger induced EMF.

items.question: Why is no EMF induced when a magnet rests motionless beside a coil?
items.expectedAnswer: The flux through the coil is not changing.
items.explanation: Induction needs a CHANGING flux; a motionless magnet produces a steady flux and no EMF.
options: The magnet has lost its field.
The flux through the coil is not changing.
The coil has too few turns.

items.question: A bar magnet is moved in and out of a coil repeatedly. The induced current...
items.expectedAnswer: alternates direction (reverses each time the motion reverses).
items.explanation: As the flux increases then decreases, the induced current reverses direction — an alternating current.
options: alternates direction (reverses each time the motion reverses).

items.question: Two identical magnets move into two coils at the same speed; coil X has 100 turns and coil Y has 50 turns. Which has the larger induced EMF?
items.expectedAnswer: Coil X (more turns).
items.explanation: EMF increases with the number of turns, so coil X (100 turns) has the larger EMF.

items.question: Why does spinning a coil faster in a generator produce a higher EMF?
items.expectedAnswer: The flux through the coil changes more rapidly.
items.explanation: Faster rotation means the flux changes faster, increasing the induced EMF.
options: The flux through the coil changes more rapidly.

items.question: Which combination would give the LARGEST induced EMF?
items.expectedAnswer: A strong magnet, many turns and fast motion.
items.explanation: Induced EMF grows with field strength, number of turns and rate of flux change.
options: A weak magnet, few turns and slow motion.
A strong magnet, many turns and fast motion.

items.question: A transformer relies on electromagnetic induction because...
items.expectedAnswer: a changing current in one coil produces a changing flux that induces an EMF in the second coil.
items.explanation: An alternating current in the primary makes a changing flux, inducing an EMF in the secondary — induction.
options: a changing current in one coil produces a changing flux that induces an EMF in the second coil.
a steady current induces an EMF.
the coils touch and share charge.

items.question: Moving a coil sideways past a magnet's pole induces a current because...
items.expectedAnswer: the flux through the coil changes as it moves.
items.explanation: Relative motion changes the flux linking the coil, inducing an EMF and current.
options: the coil gains charge from the magnet.
the flux through the coil changes as it moves.

items.question: What happens to the induced EMF if a magnet is moved into a coil and then withdrawn at the same speed?
items.expectedAnswer: The EMF reverses direction on withdrawal.
items.explanation: Inserting increases flux and withdrawing decreases it, so the induced EMF (and current) reverses.
options: The EMF stays in the same direction.
No EMF is induced on withdrawal.
The EMF reverses direction on withdrawal.

items.question: Electromagnetic induction is the principle behind which device?
items.expectedAnswer: An electrical generator.
items.explanation: Generators use electromagnetic induction to produce electricity from motion.

items.question: If a coil is connected to a sensitive meter and a magnet is held perfectly still inside it, the meter reads...
items.expectedAnswer: zero.
items.explanation: No flux change means no induced EMF, so the meter reads zero.
